name: MoshiRAG
access: Self-hosted from Hugging Face: PyTorch bf16 and Rust/Candle bf16 builds of the Moshika-based front end, with a separate retrieval back end

voice.input_audio: 24 kHz mono through the Mimi codec, as for Moshi; a separate streaming speech-recognition service must transcribe the user so the retrieval back end gets context [kyutai-card-moshirag]
voice.output_audio: 24 kHz mono through the Mimi codec, as for Moshi [kyutai-card-moshirag]
voice.voices: 1 fixed synthetic voice (Moshika); the model is trained to produce one voice only, to avoid impersonation [kyutai-card-moshirag]
voice.turn_detection: None to configure; the model keeps listening and speaking, as Moshi does [kyutai-card-moshirag]
voice.interruption: Built into the full-duplex front end; no setting exists; while retrieval runs the model can say short acknowledgments or coarse answers so the talk stays natural [kyutai-card-moshirag]
voice.latency: No end-to-end figure read; the front end is Moshi's; the README says the system is sensitive to retrieval latencies above 3 seconds [kyutai-gh-moshirag]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: Open weights with no hosted price. The README asks for a GPU with 24 GB or more for the PyTorch front end, optionally a second GPU for the reference encoder or the retrieval model, and a retrieval back end such as a local vLLM server or an OpenAI-compatible API [kyutai-gh-moshirag]
